{{Short description|Link between differential equations and integrable systems}}
In [[mathematical physics]], the '''ODE/IM correspondence''' is a link between [[ordinary differential equation]]s (ODEs) and [[integrable system|integrable model]]s. It was first found in 1998 by Patrick Dorey and Roberto Tateo.<ref name="DT">{{cite journal 
|last1=Dorey |first1=Patrick 
|last2=Tateo |first2=Roberto 
|title=Anharmonic oscillators, the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz and nonlinear integral equations 
|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General |date=24 September 1999 
|volume=32 |issue=38 |pages=L419–L425 
|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/32/38/102 
|arxiv=hep-th/9812211}}</ref> In this original setting it relates the [[spectral theory|spectrum]] of a certain integrable model of [[magnetism]] known as the [[quantum Heisenberg model|XXZ-model]] to solutions of the one-dimensional [[Schrödinger equation]] with a specific choice of potential, where the position coordinate is considered as a complex coordinate.

Since then, such a correspondence has been found for many more ODE/IM pairs.<ref name="DDT">{{cite journal 
|last1=Dorey |first1=Patrick 
|last2=Dunning |first2=Clare 
|last3=Tateo |first3=Roberto 
|title=The ODE/IM correspondence 
|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical |date=10 August 2007 
|volume=40 |issue=32 |pages=R205–R283 
|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/40/32/R01 
|arxiv=hep-th/0703066 
|s2cid=14281617 
}}</ref>
